tim_output.campaign_summary: Black Basta is a ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS) variant first identified in April 2022 that has impacted over 500 organizations globally across at least 12 of 16 critical infrastructure sectors, including the Healthcare and Public Health sector. Black Basta affiliates employ common initial access techniques such as spearphishing and exploitation of known vulnerabilities (including CVE-2024-1709), followed by a double-extortion model that encrypts systems and exfiltrates data using tools like RClone, with ransom demands delivered via Tor-based leak sites. The threat actors use legitimate tools (AnyDesk, Cobalt Strike, PsExec) combined with credential scraping and privilege escalation exploits (Mimikatz, ZeroLogon, NoPac, PrintNightmare) to establish persistence and lateral movement across victim networks.
